messages:
maria-dev: Quick question — planning to reduce inference-statefulset from 6 -> 3 for low traffic window today. Also want to bump CPU/memory on the canary pods to validate performance. Plan is to change via Terraform (module.inference.replicas = 3) and update k8s template with new resources and a rollingUpdate partition. Anyone see gotchas with PVC attachments, ordinals, or TF ordering?

ryan-k8s: If it's a StatefulSet with PVs, lowering replicas will delete the highest ordinals. Make sure PVC reclaimPolicy is what you expect (Retain if you need the data). For the canary, use partitioned RollingUpdate: set spec.updateStrategy.rollingUpdate.partition to keep the canary pod(s) stable while you adjust the template.

chen-ops: A couple of infra notes: 1) PodDisruptionBudget can block scale-down if minAvailable too high. 2) Check for an HPA — if present it may fight TF-set replicas. 3) If you’re using dynamic provisioning, confirm reclaimPolicy so we don't lose cache volumes.

sam-sre: We've seen a case where reducing a statefulset removed PVCs with Delete reclaimPolicy during an infra tweak. Recommend snapshotting any important volumes first. Also consider increasing terminationGracePeriodSeconds to allow graceful eviction of worker processes.

maria-dev: Thanks. For the canary resource bump I planned to patch the manifest and trigger a canary release with partition=1 (one upgraded pod). Example snippet I was going to apply: ```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: StatefulSet
spec:
  updateStrategy:
    type: RollingUpdate
    rollingUpdate:
      partition: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: inference
        resources:
          requests:
            cpu: "2"
            memory: 8Gi
          limits:
            cpu: "4"
            memory: 12Gi
```
Is that fine or should we do something different?

ryan-k8s: That looks fine. A couple extra tips: add a more conservative readinessProbe timeout (slow-start) so the new pod isn't killed before the JVM/GPU warmup completes. Also bump terminationGracePeriodSeconds (~120s) so it gets time to flush caches.

maria-dev: For the Terraform diff I'm seeing: module.inference.k8s_manifest replicas: 6 -> 3 and resources changed. Do we want to do a two-step approach (partition + template, then scale replicas) or apply both together?

chen-ops: Two-step is safer: 1) apply the new template but keep partition = currentReplicas (e.g., 6) so nothing restarts, 2) scale replicas down to 3, 3) set partition = 3 to rollout the template to the remaining pods. That avoids mass churn and accidental simultaneous PV deletes.

sam-sre: Also: add an annotation in the PR describing the exact step order + contact list. I'll watch etcd/kubelet events during the window. We'll snapshot PVCs just in case.

maria-dev: @sam-sre @ryan-k8s ok I'll open the TF PR and include the step-by-step runbook. Quick Q: could HPA auto-scale after we finish and create extra pods that defeat the scale down? How do we temporarily stop that?

ryan-k8s: If there's an HPA, set minReplicas=maxReplicas=3 temporarily, or pause it if your HPA controller supports an annotation (e.g., autoscaler.k8s.io/paused=true). I wouldn't point scaleTargetRef to an invalid target — that can have weird side effects.

chen-ops: Another option is to set the HPA target CPU/metrics high so it won't trigger during the window, but min=max is the cleanest. Make sure you restore the original HPA after.

maria-dev: Perfect — plan is: 1) open TF PR with new template (partition set to 6), 2) patch HPA to min=max=3, 3) terraform apply replicas=3, 4) set partition=3 to rollout resources to remaining pods, 5) restore HPA, 6) verify PVs and app telemetry. Scheduling for 13:00 PT. @deploy-bot can you create a rollback/incident draft if PV errors pop up?

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Created incident draft #INF-298 for potential PV rollback. Assigned to @sam-sre. ETA 13:00 PT.

sam-sre: I'll be online for the window and watching pod/PVC events. Ping me when the PR is merged to staging so I can tail logs.

maria-dev: Thanks all :thumbsup:
